data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, is currently valued at $1.0B post-money following $700M in total raised capital. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Amogy ($700M Series C), and Redwood Materials ($6.0B Series D)—alongside 1 public comparable and 8 additional private peers in climate and energy infrastructure.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using a standard 1.7x multiplier for Series C advancement, implies a $1.7B valuation. Peer-median analysis across the three primary comparables yields $3.0B, reflecting the wide dispersion in the sector ($700M to $6.0B range). The peer universe exhibits substantial valuation volatility, with Amogy at the low end and Redwood Materials commanding 8.6x the floor valuation.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.3B. The current $1.0B valuation sits substantially below this range, suggesting upside on a forward-looking basis. Key uncertainties include technology de-risking milestones, commercialization timelines, and the broader cost trajectory for hydrogen electrolysis equipment—factors that substantially differentiate valuations even within this narrow peer cohort.
